comparison: Perfect agreement on chip-generated resistant cells (C7-C36, C146-C151). Both evaluations find the technological approach convincing and the generation of L-DOXR cells well-supported by temporal progression, spatial distribution, FACS analysis, and IC50 measurements.

Complete agreement on in vitro and in vivo characterization of resistant cells (C37-C46). Both evaluations affirm the enhanced proliferation, migration, and carcinogenesis demonstrated through multiple assays with statistical significance, particularly emphasizing the xenograft validation.

Agreement on clinical relevance through tissue microarray analysis (C47-C51). Both evaluations recognize the correlation between large cells and tumor grade in patient tissues, though both note limitations (OpenEval: C51 is inferential; Peer: single cell line model).

Strong agreement on NUPR1 identification (C52-C63). Both evaluations support the RNA-seq discovery, pathway analysis, validation experiments, and clinical correlation through Kaplan-Meier analysis. The unbiased genome-wide approach is recognized as a strength by both.

Agreement on NUPR1 functional validation (C64-C69) with peer review also including therapeutic validation claims (C71-C77). Both affirm bidirectional evidence through knockdown and overexpression experiments. Peer review notes lack of mechanistic detail about how NUPR1 functionally imparts resistance.

OpenEval addresses ZZW-115 therapeutic validation (C70-C77) while peer review combines this with functional validation. Both support dose-dependent re-sensitization in vitro and tumor reduction in vivo, confirming the therapeutic potential of NUPR1 inhibition.

Agreement on epigenetic mechanism (C78-C84). Both evaluations support the evidence for H3K27 acetylation, HDAC11 loss, and the regulatory relationship. OpenEval finds mechanistic inference well-supported; peer review acknowledges the epigenetic regulation but notes downstream mechanism remains unclear.

Agreement on HDAC11 as direct NUPR1 regulator (C85-C90). Both evaluations support the bidirectional evidence from overexpression and inhibition experiments establishing HDAC11's regulatory role, though peer review emphasizes the gap in understanding how NUPR1 confers resistance.

Complete agreement on clinical validation of NUPR1/HDAC11 axis (C91-C95). Both evaluations affirm the tissue microarray and Kaplan-Meier analyses demonstrating grade-dependent expression and survival correlation, strengthening clinical relevance.

Divergent evaluations on mechanistic completeness (C100-C103, C119-C129). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED, finding the HDAC11→NUPR1 regulatory mechanism complete. Peer review rates as UNCERTAIN, explicitly noting 'absolutely no mechanistic insights into how NUPR1 functionally imparts resistance'—the downstream mechanism is incomplete.

Agreement on background literature (C131-C139) with peer review also addressing platform value (C140, C143). Both recognize appropriate contextualization of PACCs/PGCCs literature. Peer review additionally affirms the CDRA chip's value as a platform technology.

OpenEval rates predictive capability claims (C140, C143-C145) as UNCERTAIN due to lack of prospective validation. Peer review rates platform value claims (C140, C143) as SUPPORTED, emphasizing the technique's capability for understanding chemoresistance mechanisms.

Partial overlap on background claims. OpenEval addresses platform predictive claims (C140, C143-C145) as UNCERTAIN. Peer review addresses broader background context (C1-C6, C96-C99, C141-C145) as SUPPORTED, treating these as uncontroversial contextual statements.

Agreement on background and context claims (C1-C6, C96-C98). Both evaluations treat these as well-established facts supported by appropriate citations that provide necessary scientific rationale but are not primary findings under evaluation.

Agreement on NUPR1 background literature (C11-C16). Both evaluations affirm these are established literature claims supported by citations that appropriately contextualize NUPR1's relevance as a target.

Agreement on HDAC11 background literature (C17-C26, C104-C118). Both evaluations support the comprehensive review of HDAC11's complex roles across cancers, with appropriate acknowledgment of contradictory findings in different cancer types.

Partial overlap on HDAC11 findings in this study (C116-C118). OpenEval includes these in broader literature review as SUPPORTED. Peer review groups these with interpretive claims as SUPPORTED, recognizing they flow logically from experimental findings.
Agreement on therapeutic rationale claims (C123-C126). Both evaluations support these background claims about targeting histone modifications as established literature providing context.

Agreement on interpretive claim C130. Both evaluations support the inference that HDACi evaluation should consider drug resistance context, recognizing this as appropriate interpretation of the study's implications.

Agreement on speculative claim C122. Both evaluations recognize this as appropriately qualified speculation about HDAC11 suppression mechanism that requires further investigation. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN; peer review rates as SUPPORTED given appropriate qualification.
